//: Two agents, not three. A `glm-explore` child agent was written and removed: OpenCode 1.18.16 offers no subagent-delegation tool over the server API. Even the built-in `build` agent lists only apply_patch, bash, edit, glob, grep, question, read, skill, todowrite, webfetch and websearch, so there is nothing for a parent to delegate through. Setting `permission.task` or `tools.task` changes nothing. subagent_depth is kept at 1 so nested agents stay capped if a later version enables them. The child-session discovery in the runtime is also kept: it reports what actually ran rather than what an agent claims, and returns an empty list until this works.
//permissions: bash has NO allow rules, deliberately. Two facts force this. First, OpenCode resolves the LAST matching rule, so a trailing catch-all silently overrides every allow and deny above it: with `*` last, `git status --short` prompted despite an explicit allow and `curl` was downgraded from deny to merely approvable. Second, with the catch-all moved first, the remaining allow patterns became real allows over arbitrary arguments, and a read-only agent ran `cat C:/Users/<user>/canary.txt` and returned its contents with no prompt. `external_directory: deny` does not cover bash. A glob over a command string cannot confine a path, so no allow pattern here is safe and none is offered. This costs less than it appears: OpenCode's own read, grep, glob and list tools ARE confined by external_directory, so the agent has proper repo-scoped tools and only needs bash for things a person should see anyway. The catch-all is `ask` rather than `deny` because a shell command that writes cannot be told from one that reads by pattern, so a human decides.

external-builder.description: Primary external worker with write access inside one repository.

external-researcher.description: Read-only external worker. Investigates and reports, never edits.
